newsitem.title: USA: Navistar Canadian workers ratify contract.
newsitem.headline: Navistar Canadian workers ratify contract.

text.p: Navistar International Corp said Tuesday its Chatham, Ontario, employees represented by the Canadian Auto Workers Local 127 voted to ratify a new three-year labor agreement.
The contract becomes effective immediately and will extend through October 1999.

The contract, covering 1,300 out of 1,600 workers at its Chatham facility, includes a two percent increase in wages in each of the next three years. These costs will be offset by work rule changes designed to improve productivity and increase quality, Navistar said.
In addition, the contract allows Navistar to proceed with product and facility initiatives aimed at reducing costs significantly, the company said.

"We recognize, however, that more work needs to be done over the long term to align Navistar's wage and benefit structure with those of our major competitors in the truck manufacturing industry," said John Horne, Navistar chairman. "Going forward, we will work closely with union leadership to do so."
Navistar makes buses, medium- and heavy-duty trucks and diesel engines.
